audit: CK6 sharded target enumeration - sharding/count prefilter bug
status: bug confirmed; repair designed; regression test ALL PASS; no large search launched; no historical artefact modified

root_cause.defect: candidate minimum-orbit ids are admitted only if reachable from a start-front orbit s0 through adjacent orbits with ids >= s0 (id-nondecreasing from the chain ROOT). This assumes orbit ids (l1_ball enumeration order) are compatible with centre-outward connectivity growth, which is false. The seeded DFS itself only needs ids >= s from the seed s onward, so valid min-ids below the centre-adjacent orbits' ids are wrongly excluded.
root_cause.false_assumption: every connected CK6-closed target's minimum orbit id is reachable centre-outward through non-decreasing orbit ids

old_vs_corrected.old: s admitted iff s reachable FROM a start-front orbit via ids >= s0 (root-bounded)
old_vs_corrected.corrected: s admitted iff s can REACH a start-front orbit via adjacent orbits with ids >= s (sound necessary condition; over-approximation harmless); or simply use all orbit ids as the shard domain
old_vs_corrected.completeness_proof: Disjoint: min orbit id is intrinsic; shard s enumerates exactly {T : minid(T)=s}. Complete: every connected CK6-closed odd-volume target contains its inversion-centre cell and has orbit cost exactly (V-1)/2; its orbit graph is connected with all ids >= s, so a frontier growth order from {centre, s} exists; the frontier is a function of the mask so visited-dedup is sound; hence iter_targets_seeded(un, s, (V-1)//2) yields it. The corrected filter keeps every s satisfying the necessary condition, so no target's shard is dropped.
